import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 616

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/616](https://www.erdosproblems.com/616)
- [EHT91] Erdős, Paul and Hajnal, András and Tuza, Zsolt, Local constraints ensuring small
  representing sets. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1991), 78-84.
-/

namespace Erdos616

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $r\geq 3$. For an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$ let $\tau(G)$ denote the covering number (or
transversal number), the minimum size of a set of vertices which includes at least one from each
edge in $G$. Determine the best possible $t$ such that, if $G$ is an $r$-uniform hypergraph $G$
where every subgraph $G'$ on at most $3r-3$ vertices has $\tau(G')\leq 1$, we have $\tau(G)\leq t$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_616 :
    let f : ℕ → ℕ∞ := answer(sorry)
    ∀ r : ℕ, 3 ≤ r → Hypergraph.localTransversalBound r (3 * r - 3) 1 = f r := by
  sorry

end Erdos616

reformulations.difference: The source asks for the best global transversal bound under a condition on every small subgraph. Lean tests induced vertex sets and expresses the answer as an ℕ∞ infimum of admissible natural-number global bounds.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A transversal for an induced hypergraph also covers every edge-deleting subgraph on the same vertices; conversely, induced hypergraphs are among those subgraphs. Transversal witnesses may be restricted to the specified vertex set by intersection without increasing cardinality. The defining infimum equals b precisely when b is an admissible universal bound and is no larger than every other admissible bound. Moreover, for r ≥ 3, any two edges occupy at most 2r ≤ 3r−3 vertices, so the local condition forces them to intersect. Any edge therefore supplies a global transversal of size r; the empty hypergraph has transversal size zero. Thus the infimum is finite and represents exactly the source's best possible t. The local-condition equivalence and the combined least-bound equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/616?source=1 (read through Jina Reader; exact mathematical statement and cited bounds)
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html (archive index consulted while seeking EHT91)
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem, its answer-function scope, and all definitions used by localTransversalBound. The source still records OPEN. Scratch proofs establish the least-bound interpretation and 1 ≤ localTransversalBound r (3*r−3) 1 ≤ r for every r ≥ 3, without using the problem's sorry theorem. Boundary tests cover the empty vertex type, empty families, empty edges, a single triple, and two disjoint triples. An executable 6-uniform example also satisfies the local constraint while requiring two transversal vertices. The reviewed file matches the specified committed version. EHT91's full text could not be retrieved despite publisher/archive attempts; its bibliographic metadata was verified, and statement faithfulness was settled against the exact Erdős Problems LaTeX text.
